bh.name: Brighton & Hove
bh.rule: Catchment areas, then a random lottery within bands (siblings, free school meals, catchment, open)
bh.towns: Brighton, Hove, Portslade, Patcham, Woodingdean, Rottingdean, Saltdean
bh.edge: Peacehaven and Newhaven families often list Longhill from over the border — it's usually undersubscribed.

hastings.name: Hastings, Bexhill & Rye
hastings.towns: Hastings, St Leonards, Bexhill-on-Sea, Battle, Rye, Robertsbridge and the surrounding villages
hastings.edge: The gap between the town schools and St Richard's or Claverham is the widest in the tool — worth reading the numbers before ranking on convenience.

wealden.name: Uckfield, Crowborough & Heathfield
wealden.towns: Uckfield, Crowborough, Heathfield, Hailsham, Chailey, Ringmer and the Wealden villages
wealden.edge: Rural distances dominate here: for many villages the nearest school and the best-rated school are not the same bus.

eastbourne.name: Eastbourne, Willingdon & Langney
eastbourne.towns: Eastbourne, Old Town, Meads, Hampden Park, Langney, Willingdon and Stone Cross
eastbourne.edge: Gildredge House is 4-16, so its own primary children transfer up and fewer Year 7 places reach outside applicants than the roll suggests.

lewes.name: Lewes, Newhaven, Peacehaven & Seaford
lewes.rule: Community areas, then distance — no lottery; your address decides continuously
lewes.towns: Lewes, Newhaven, Peacehaven, Telscombe, Seaford and the surrounding villages
lewes.edge: Peacehaven and Telscombe sit right on the Brighton boundary — Longhill is a genuine option and appears in your list.

chichester.name: Chichester, Bognor & Littlehampton
chichester.rule: Catchment, then distance — no lottery, on a three-preference form
chichester.towns: Chichester, Bognor Regis, Felpham, Barnham, Littlehampton, Angmering, Steyning, Midhurst and the Downs villages
chichester.edge: The two faith schools — Bishop Luffa and St Philip Howard — sit clearly above the rest on results, so for many families here the practical question is whether a faith application is open to them.

crawley.name: Crawley & Horsham
crawley.rule: Catchment, then distance — no lottery, on a three-preference form
crawley.towns: Crawley, Three Bridges, Maidenbower, Ifield, Horsham, Billingshurst and the Horsham villages
crawley.edge: Horsham splits by sex at 11 — Millais for girls, The Forest for boys — so for many Horsham families the real choice is Tanbridge House or a single-sex school.

midsussex.name: Haywards Heath, Burgess Hill & Hassocks
midsussex.rule: Catchment, then distance — no lottery, on a three-preference form
midsussex.towns: Haywards Heath, Lindfield, Cuckfield, Burgess Hill, Hassocks, Hurstpierpoint, Ditchling and the Mid Sussex villages
midsussex.edge: Hassocks and Ditchling are 15 minutes from Brighton by train — but Brighton allocates on catchment first, so cross-boundary offers there are rare.

adur.name: Shoreham, Lancing & Worthing
adur.rule: Catchment, then distance — no lottery, and the form gives you three preferences, not four
adur.towns: Shoreham-by-Sea, Southwick, Lancing, Sompting, Worthing, Durrington
adur.edge: Portslade and west Hove are the boundary here — PACA sits just over it and takes some Southwick families.

kent.name: Tunbridge Wells & Tonbridge
kent.rule: Selective — grammar places go to children who pass the Kent Test, then by distance; everything else is distance-only
kent.towns: Tunbridge Wells, Tonbridge, Southborough, Paddock Wood and the villages
kent.edge: Kent is the one selective county in this tool. The Kent Test is sat in September of Year 6 — registration closes at the start of July, before the school form even opens — and it splits the district in two: six grammars averaging 70-79 Attainment 8, and six non-selective schools averaging 40-56.

maidstone.edge: 4 of these 13 schools are grammars. The offer rates shown are the real 2026 figures — the share of families who put a school first and were offered a place.

verified.kent-test: KCC: registration 1 June–1 July, test September of Year 6, results mid-October, CAF 31 October, offers 1 March; grammars provide for about the top 25% of the ability range; Kent Test valid for Kent grammars only (Medway and Bexley run separate tests) — checked 13 Aug 2026
verified.kent-prefs: KCC: up to 4 preferences on the secondary form — checked 13 Aug 2026
verified.kent-catchment: KCC/scheme: most Kent secondaries do not use traditional catchment areas; allocation is each school's own oversubscription criteria, usually distance — consistent with our nomap treatment
verified.surrey-prefs: Surrey CC Admission Arrangements 2027/28: applicants rank UP TO SIX preferences for secondary (we had four) — checked 13 Aug 2026
verified.surrey-tiebreak: Surrey CC 2027/28: where two children are equidistant, priority is decided by a randomly assigned computer-generated number
verified.hants-prefs: Hampshire CC: name up to THREE schools on the Year 7 application — checked 13 Aug 2026
verified.hants-catchment: Hampshire CC catchment finder: all community and VC schools have a designated catchment; some own-admission schools use none; SOME ADDRESSES ARE IN CATCHMENT FOR MORE THAN ONE SCHOOL — checked 13 Aug 2026
verified.hants-open-data: Hampshire publishes school catchment polygons as open data (data.gov.uk, OS Open Data Licence) — the only authority in the build that does; SHP download at hants.gov.uk opendata
